title_en: The $9B Portfolio That Fits on One Page
title_zh: 能写在一页纸上的 90 亿美元组合 | North Dakota Trust Lands 首席投资官 Frank Mihail
subtitle_zh: Frank Mihail 谈如何用三人团队、约 40 个持仓条目，管好 90 亿美元主权财富基金。
summary_zh: 本期 Swimming with Allocators 由 Alexa Binns 与 Earnest Sweat 对话 North Dakota Trust Lands 首席投资官（CIO）Frank Mihail，他用仅三人的团队、约 40 个持仓条目，管好 North Dakota 主权财富基金与永久基金里约 90 亿美元的资产——一个更接近 Texas Permanent、Alaska Permanent 模式、而非传统养老金的组合，其能写在一页纸上的配置正是本集看点。Mihail 在 Los Angeles 长大，从油气工程师、房地产中介（恰逢 2008 年金融危机转做不良地产）到财富管理，考下 CFA、读完 UCLA MBA，近 40 岁时赴 New Mexico PERA 负责对冲基金组合、搭建可转移阿尔法（portable alpha）计划，2023 年才举家搬到 North Dakota。他接手时该计划私募市场极年轻、流动性很高，几乎是一张白纸，且五人董事会（由民选官员组成）近年更替进更愿承担风险的成员，时机刚好推动另类（alts）策略落地。基金收入来自全州土地出租与石油特许权使用费，本身对组合构成天然对冲，是全美最健康的计划之一，过去三年从约 60 亿做到 90 亿美元。节目还讨论内部托管 SMA 与外部共同基金（commingled fund）的取舍、新兴管理人对 McKinsey 式商业咨询的需要，以及体育资产因稀缺性成为另类投资热点的逻辑。

turns.en: You ready? Let's dive in. Today's episode, we have Frank Mihail, Chief Investment Officer at North Dakota Trust Lands. He's the CIO overseeing roughly $9 billion across North Dakota's sovereign wealth and permanent funds.
turns.zh: 准备好了吗？我们开始吧。今天这期节目，我们请到了 Frank Mihail，他是 North Dakota Trust Lands 的首席投资官（CIO）。作为 CIO，他掌管着 North Dakota 主权财富基金和永久基金里大约 90 亿美元的资产。

turns.en: So you can think of this as a model closer to the Texas Permanent and Alaska Permanent funds than a traditional pension. We're so eager to have you.
turns.zh: 所以你可以把它理解成一种更接近 Texas Permanent 和 Alaska Permanent 基金的模式，而不是传统的养老金。我们非常期待你能来。

turns.en: Thank you, Frank, for being here. Yeah, thanks for having me, Alexa, Ernest. Pleasure to be here. We have discussed how you ended up in North Dakota.
turns.zh: Frank，谢谢你能来。嗯，谢谢你们邀请我，Alexa、Ernest，很荣幸来到这里。（此前）我们聊过你是怎么一路来到 North Dakota 的。

turns.en: We've got a shared alma mater at UCLA. And what it took to convince your family they wanted to meet up in North Dakota. Can you bring us on this journey of how you have ended up where you are?
turns.zh: 我们还是 UCLA 的校友。也聊了你要怎么说服家人愿意搬到 North Dakota。你能带我们走一遍这段历程吗——你是怎么一步步走到今天这个位置的？

turns.en: Yeah, well, I grew up in Los Angeles and started my career in the oil and gas industry as an engineer. At that time, like 2006 pre-GFC, everybody around me was making money in real estate in Los Angeles.
turns.zh: 嗯，我是在 Los Angeles 长大的，职业生涯是从油气行业起步的，做工程师。那时候大概是 2006 年，全球金融危机（GFC）之前，我身边所有人都在 Los Angeles 靠房地产赚钱。

turns.en: And so I started moonlighting as a real estate agent. And my timing was impeccable. By the time I went full time into real estate sales, it was 2008.
turns.zh: 于是我就开始兼职做房地产中介。而我这个时机把握得真是‘无懈可击’——等我全职转做房地产销售的时候，已经是 2008 年了。

turns.en: And so I started learning about distressed real estate investing in apartment buildings. And that was sort of my first taste into investing.
turns.zh: 所以我就开始学习不良（distressed）房地产投资，主要是公寓楼。那算是我第一次尝到投资的滋味。

turns.en: And I wanted to learn more about investing. So I pivoted from real estate to wealth management when I was 30 years old. And I was hungry to learn.
turns.zh: 而我想更深入地学投资。所以在 30 岁那年，我从房地产转行做财富管理（wealth management）。我当时特别渴望学习。

turns.en: So I got the CFA. I enrolled at the UCLA MBA program. And I used that to pivot into institutional investing and left Southern California for the first time in my late 30s to take a job with New Mexico Para, the public pension.
turns.zh: 于是我考下了 CFA，报了 UCLA 的 MBA 项目。我借着这个转型进入机构投资，并且在快 40 岁的时候第一次离开南加州，去 New Mexico PERA 这家公共养老金工作。

turns.en: I was covering the hedge fund portfolio over there. And yeah, I moved up pretty quick and got responsibility over the hedge fund book to build a portable alpha program.
turns.zh: 我在那边负责对冲基金组合。嗯，我升得挺快，很快就接手了对冲基金这块业务，去搭建一个可转移阿尔法（portable alpha）计划。

turns.en: And I think that experience set me up to then land the opportunity in North Dakota. And my wife is a teacher, so she can get a job anywhere in the nation in my two weeks.
turns.zh: 我觉得正是那段经历，为我后来到 North Dakota 抓住这个机会打下了基础。而且我太太是老师，所以基本上全国哪儿都能找到工作，两周之内就能上岗。

turns.en: That's true. And so yeah, we moved up to North Dakota in early 2023. And for this opportunity in North Dakota, what really drew you to it? I know you wanted your eager to learn and you've shown your aspirations throughout your career of like, oh, there's something new that seems interesting and you jump right into it.
turns.zh: 确实。所以我们是在 2023 年初搬到 North Dakota 的。那说到 North Dakota 这个机会，究竟是什么真正吸引了你？我知道你一直很好学，你整个职业生涯都展现出这样一种劲头——一看到有什么新鲜、有意思的东西，你就一头扎进去。

turns.en: What was it about this opportunity? Well, it was an opportunity to move from just focusing on hedge funds to having decision-making over the entire portfolio.
turns.zh: 这个机会到底哪里吸引你？嗯，它是一个让我从只盯着对冲基金，转变为对整个组合拥有决策权的机会。

turns.en: And I love the idea of covering all asset classes as a generalist because it never gets boring. And when I joined in 2023, a lot of the mature endowments and pensions were suffering from the denominator effect.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢作为一名通才（generalist）去覆盖所有资产类别，因为这永远不会腻。而我 2023 年加入的时候，很多成熟的捐赠基金和养老金正深受分母效应（denominator effect）之苦。

turns.en: But we have a really young private markets program and a very liquid portfolio. So I essentially inherited a blank canvas, which is like the envy of all allocators.
turns.zh: 但我们的私募市场（private markets）计划非常年轻，组合的流动性也很高。所以基本上我接手的是一张白纸，这可是所有配置者（allocator）都羡慕的东西。

turns.en: And a willingness for change. I feel like the combination of the two. Where did that come from? So where was the impetus to start an ALTS strategy?
turns.zh: 而且还有一种愿意变革的心态。我觉得是这两者的结合。这种心态是从哪儿来的呢？那么，当初启动另类（alts）策略的推动力是什么？

turns.en: Well, the history of the plan is it was very fixed income oriented. And I think over time, the board is structured as a five-person board with elected officials that are generally termed out for your terms possible reelection.
turns.zh: 嗯，这个计划的历史是它非常偏向固定收益。而且我觉得随着时间推移，董事会的架构是一个五人董事会，成员是民选官员，通常有任期限制，任期满了之后有可能连任。

turns.en: But there's turnover. So there's been new board members over the last decade that might be younger and more risk seeking or have a willingness to accept more risk in the portfolio.
turns.zh: 但人员是有更替的。所以在过去十年里，陆续有新的董事会成员加入，他们可能更年轻、更愿意承担风险，或者更乐意让组合去承受更多风险。

turns.en: And so I think the timing was sort of just aligned there. I know New Mexico has a more established alternatives program. Was there anything?
turns.zh: 所以我觉得时机刚好就对上了。我知道 New Mexico 的另类投资计划更成熟一些。那有没有……

turns.en: Have you pulled any learnings from there, having been on the outside, managing a different pot of capital? Is there, you know, those are your fellow allocators and your community.
turns.zh: 你有没有从那边汲取到什么经验？毕竟你当时是在外部、管理着另一笔不同的资金。你知道的，那些人是你的同行配置者、是你的圈子。

turns.en: Is there anything that you sort of see looking back, building your new program? Yeah, like you mentioned, the New Mexico program was more mature and built out.
turns.zh: 回过头看，在你搭建新计划的时候，有没有什么让你有所触动的？嗯，就像你说的，New Mexico 的计划更成熟、体系也更完整。

turns.en: They had been investing in private equity for 20 years and so the team was bigger. We have three people here all in, including operations. They have, I think, 10 with dedicated operations staff.
turns.zh: 他们做私募股权（private equity）投资已经 20 年了，所以团队更大。我们这边算上运营总共才三个人。他们那边我记得有 10 个人，还有专门的运营团队。

turns.en: And so they were able to manage like a 200 line item book. And we have 40 line items and we try to keep it pretty tight. And so yeah, I think one of the things I noticed when I joined over there was like, there's a lot of, like with the closed end fund investing, especially through the GFC, there was a lot of line items that had just been sitting on the books for like, well over a decade, you know, like 15 plus years.
turns.zh: 所以他们能管理一个大约有 200 个持仓条目（line item）的组合。而我们只有 40 个条目，而且尽量控制得很精简。嗯，我记得我刚到那边时注意到的一点是——尤其是在封闭式基金（closed-end fund）投资这块，特别是经历了全球金融危机之后，有很多条目就那么挂在账上，挂了远远超过十年，得有 15 年以上。

turns.en: And they might have like an asset that was distressed because of the GFC, but they was just still sitting on the books like with a million dollars.
turns.zh: 他们可能有一笔资产因为金融危机而变成了不良资产，但它就那么挂在账上，还值个一百万美元。

turns.en: And I think like cleaning up those old line items is helpful, which is why the secondary markets are around for us. So we've had a lot of people come on and talk about having a blank slate.
turns.zh: 我觉得清理这些老旧的持仓条目是有帮助的，这也正是二级市场（secondary markets）存在的意义。我们节目请过很多人来聊‘一张白纸’这个话题。

turns.en: And from some of the allocators who have been on, they've expressed some kind of hesitation to venture capital specifically because it's one that's an asset class that typically has an inverse relationship with dollars to time spent in learning.
turns.zh: 一些上过节目的配置者表示，他们对风险投资（venture capital）尤其有些犹豫，因为这个资产类别通常有个特点：投入的资金规模和花在学习上的时间往往成反比。

turns.en: How was your approach when having a blank slate specifically around like venture capital, which is a little bit different than covering hedge funds?
turns.zh: 那么，在一张白纸的情况下，你的思路是怎样的？尤其是围绕风险投资——这和做对冲基金还有点不一样。

turns.en: When I joined, yeah, we didn't have any venture in the book. And it was an area that I wanted to start adding to the portfolio. And so I was trying to figure out what's the best way to go about it.
turns.zh: 我加入的时候，对，我们组合里一点风投都没有。而这是一个我想开始往组合里增加的领域。所以我就在琢磨，用什么方式去做最合适。

turns.en: It is one of the areas where you pretty much have to do close-end fund investing. And so my focus on trying to reduce line item sprawl and add as few line items as possible, we thought about, well, we're going to have to, how do we write a large check, like a $50 million check to a manager but get access to a suite of or diversified portfolio?
turns.zh: 风投是那种你基本上必须做封闭式基金投资的领域之一。所以我一直在想着怎么减少持仓条目的蔓延、尽量少增加条目。我们就琢磨：好吧，我们要怎么才能给一个管理人开出一张大额支票——比如 5,000 万美元的支票——但同时又能拿到一整套、或者说一个分散化的组合？

turns.en: And so I think the larger platforms made more sense for us there. And so that's sort of where we started. It feels like the line item is a helpful shorthand for us as DCs to understand your perspective of what you're prioritizing and why.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得对我们来说，更大的平台更合适。我们大致就是从那儿起步的。感觉‘持仓条目’对我们这些配置者来说是个很好用的速记方式，能帮我们理解你在优先看重什么、以及为什么这么排。

turns.en: What does that represent for you, like when you describe trying to stay below 40 or 50 line items? Our entire portfolio fits on one page. And I can recite it like the back of my hand.
turns.zh: 那对你来说，当你说想把持仓条目控制在 40 或 50 个以内时，这代表着什么？我们整个组合能写在一页纸上。而且我能把它背得滚瓜烂熟。

turns.en: And I guess I don't know if all CIOs have that convenience, right? Like if you've got 1,000 line items on the book and you're like a $200 billion pension, it becomes hard to even like managing your head, right?
turns.zh: 我猜也不是所有 CIO 都有这种便利吧？如果你账上有 1,000 个持仓条目，又是一个 2,000 亿美元规模的养老金，那你光是理清头绪都难，对吧？

turns.en: And so I think there is, I've met a lot of allocators who are in that place now and now they want to come back and say, hey, let's reduce the number of relationships and have fewer relationships, higher conviction, right, bigger checks.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得……我遇到过很多配置者，现在正处在那样的境地，于是他们又想回过头来说：嘿，咱们减少合作关系的数量吧，关系少一点、信念强一点，对吧，支票开大一点。

turns.en: And so I guess we were lucky in that we didn't have to go down that path to then come back. We're sort of already a pretty concentrated book.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得我们挺幸运，不用先走上那条路、再折返回来。我们本来就已经是一个相当集中的组合了。

turns.en: And I think we want to keep it that way. I think another thing that's really interesting when we were speaking in the prep call is the structure of just North Dakota trust lands.
turns.zh: 而且我们也想一直保持这样。我觉得还有一点特别有意思——我们在预备通话里聊到的——就是 North Dakota Trust Lands 本身的这套结构。

turns.en: And I learned that it's funded by oil royalties and pays out 5% to public schools without touching principal. That's just fascinating. I was curious that, and you guys have grown about, I think, about $6 billion and $9 billion in three years and cover about a quarter of the state's education costs.
turns.zh: 我了解到，它的资金来源是石油特许权使用费（oil royalties），每年向公立学校拨付 5%，而且不动本金。这真是太有意思了。我很好奇——你们大概在三年里从 60 亿美元涨到了 90 亿美元，覆盖了全州大约四分之一的教育开支。

turns.en: This is an amazing case study. I'm curious with those numbers in relationship with actually being able to benefit the public, how does that influence your risk tolerance?
turns.zh: 这是一个非常棒的研究案例。我很好奇，在这些数字、和真正能惠及公众之间，这种关系会如何影响你的风险承受能力？

turns.en: We're pretty blessed because we're one of the healthiest plans in the nation. The way it's set up is we receive the revenue from the land owned across the state.
turns.zh: 我们挺有福气的，因为我们是全国最健康的计划之一。它的运作方式是：我们从全州范围内所拥有的土地上获得收入。

turns.en: That's both renting to farmers and oil companies. As you can imagine, the oil royalties and taxes are the bulk of the income. And that is a natural hedge for the portfolio.
turns.zh: 这既包括把地租给农民，也包括租给石油公司。你可以想见，石油特许权使用费和税费是收入的大头。而这本身对组合来说就是一种天然的对冲。

turns.en: And I'll use the year 2022 as an example. In 2022, when stocks were down 20% and bonds were down 10%, our portfolio was down 8%. We use private markets and long short strategies to try to mitigate that downside.
turns.zh: 我拿 2022 年举个例子。2022 年，股票跌了 20%、债券跌了 10% 的时候，我们的组合跌了 8%。我们用私募市场和多空（long/short）策略来尽量缓冲这种下行。

turns.en: But our nav actually only went down 2.5% because of the boon we got from the oil royalties coming in. In a year like 2022, when it's driven by inflation, that was actually our best year on the revenue side of the state owned lands.
turns.zh: 但我们的净资产值（NAV）实际上只下跌了 2.5%，因为进来的石油特许权使用费给我们带来了一笔意外之财。像 2022 年这种由通胀驱动的年份，反而是我们州属土地收入端表现最好的一年。

turns.en: And so because we are an endowment and not a pension, we don't have any liabilities. We do have the ability to take risk. And so even though today, I think our asset allocation looks pretty comparable to more pensions.
turns.zh: 所以，因为我们是捐赠基金（endowment）而不是养老金，我们没有任何负债。我们确实有能力去承担风险。因此，尽管今天我觉得我们的资产配置看起来和大多数养老金差不多。

turns.en: And so one of my goals is to start incrementally taking a little bit more risk. So last summer, we did a strategic asset allocation review and moved a little bit from credit to equity.
turns.zh: 所以我的目标之一，就是开始循序渐进地多承担一点风险。去年夏天，我们做了一次战略资产配置（strategic asset allocation）评估，把一小部分从信用债挪到了股票。

turns.en: Are there any other intricacies or unique elements that you would want managers to know when approaching you based on this process that you go through?
turns.zh: 在你走这套流程的时候，还有没有什么细节或独特之处，是你希望管理人在接触你之前先了解的？

turns.en: Like are there things that are helpful for them to understand how decisions are made? I think it's not too different from most plans. Our board, we meet like 10 times a year, which is just a little less than monthly.
turns.zh: 比如说，有没有一些东西能帮他们理解决策是怎么做出来的？我觉得和大多数计划没什么太大差别。我们董事会一年大概开 10 次会，也就是比每月一次稍微少一点。

turns.en: And then our process, usually we like to have about three months to diligence a manager. And then it usually takes us like a month to get through legal after board approval.
turns.zh: 然后我们的流程是这样的：通常我们希望有大约三个月的时间去尽调（diligence）一个管理人。董事会批准之后，走法务流程通常还要花我们大约一个月。

turns.en: And yeah, I actually don't have investment discretion like some other plans. And so that means I do have to bring every recommendation to our board for approval.
turns.zh: 而且，对，我其实不像有些其他计划那样拥有投资自主权（investment discretion）。这意味着我确实得把每一条建议都提交给董事会审批。

turns.en: And because of the cadence of meeting frequently, like every month, it hasn't created any issues for me in terms of meeting fund closing deadlines or anything like that.
turns.zh: 而且因为我们开会频率很高、基本每月一次，所以在赶基金关账（closing）截止时间这类事情上，从没给我造成过什么问题。

turns.en: No, that seems remarkably fast, actually. There are some public record constraints, I believe. What should managers know about a public plan in that case?
turns.zh: 不，这其实已经算非常快了。我记得公共记录方面会有一些限制。那么在这种情况下，管理人应该了解公共计划的哪些特点？

turns.en: Yeah, yes, because we are a public plan. We are subject to FOIA public records requests. And so most of our managers who work with us are aware of that.
turns.zh: 对，是的，因为我们是公共计划，我们要接受《信息自由法》（FOIA）下的公共记录申请。所以和我们合作的大多数管理人都清楚这一点。

turns.en: And there are state laws that protect managers who are sensitive to certain information, confidentiality about their underlying deals. We do have the ability to protect that information for them.
turns.zh: 而且州法律会保护那些对某些信息敏感的管理人——涉及其底层交易（underlying deals）的保密信息。我们确实有能力替他们保护这些信息。

turns.en: So one thing I was enamored by, it was a lot of things I was enamored by when we first spoke, but you run a $9 billion plan with a three-person team.
turns.zh: 有一件事让我特别着迷——其实我们第一次聊的时候有很多东西都让我着迷——但你们只用一个三人团队，就管着一个 90 亿美元的计划。

turns.en: And so tell us about it. You're so chill. I think that's the answer. Tell us how we've heard the 40 line items on one page. That's one. But is the efficiency, you just have some stellar?
turns.zh: 那就跟我们讲讲吧。你心态也太淡定了，我觉得这就是答案。说说看是怎么做到的——我们已经听说了‘40 个持仓条目写在一页纸上’，这是第一点。但这效率……是不是因为你有一批特别出色的团队成员？

turns.en: I know you have some stellar people. Is it AI too? What's going on? Yeah, I got a stellar team. I wish we were more on the front lines of AI than we are, but we're getting up to speed.
turns.zh: 我知道你手下有一些很出色的人。是不是也用上了 AI？到底怎么回事？嗯，我确实有一支很棒的团队。真希望我们在 AI 方面能更走在前线一点，不过我们正在迎头赶上。

turns.en: One of the first things I did when I joined, and just to simplify my life, for the public stocks and bonds, they can be set up where you're in a coming of fund externally or a lot of allocators have internal SMAs where they're custodied internally at their custody bank.
turns.zh: 我加入后做的头几件事之一，纯粹是为了让自己的日子简单点：对于公开市场的股票和债券，你可以选择投到外部的共同基金（commingled fund）里，也有很多配置者用的是内部 SMA（独立管理账户），资产托管在自己的托管银行。

turns.en: There's pros and cons to both. When they're custodied internally, you get the liquidity as soon as you sell. It's already in your hands, in your possession.
turns.zh: 两种方式各有利弊。当资产是内部托管时，你一卖出就能拿到流动性，钱已经在你手上、在你手里了。

turns.en: And so you get, I guess, a day quicker liquidity. But from an operations standpoint and a counting standpoint, like closing the books every month and doing your annual audit, if you have a bond portfolio, you literally have to reconcile like 1,000 bonds.
turns.zh: 所以你的流动性大概能快一天。但从运营和记账的角度看——比如每月结账、做年度审计——如果你有一个债券组合，你就得实打实地去对账，对上千只债券。

turns.en: And I just like, you know what, I can't spend my time doing that. Like, I need to outsource that. And so we had a few of those internally-custody SMAs.
turns.zh: 我就想，算了，我可不能把时间花在这上面，我得把这块外包出去。所以我们当时有几只内部托管的 SMA。

turns.en: And I converted those to external commingled funds. And it makes my life a lot easier, having to spend less time thinking about operations and accounting.
turns.zh: 我把它们都转成了外部的共同基金。这让我轻松多了，不用花那么多时间去操心运营和会计的事。

turns.en: And that way, I can focus more on investing. I believe you also lean on some consultants and fund of funds to extend reach. How did you decide not only when to add layers of fees versus go direct, but who to do that for you?
turns.zh: 这样一来，我就能把更多精力放在投资上。我记得你们也会借助一些顾问和母基金（fund of funds）来延伸触角。你是怎么决定的——不只是什么时候该多叠一层费用、什么时候直接投，还包括让谁来替你做这件事？

turns.en: To keep a concentrated book, we have to write a large check, right? And so our minimum check size has grown as our portfolio. I mean, a lot has grown, but you guys are something.
turns.zh: 要保持一个集中的组合，我们就必须开大额支票，对吧？所以随着组合增长，我们的最低支票规模也在往上走。我是说，规模涨了不少，不过你们也确实厉害。

turns.en: So yeah, that makes sense directionally. I think like $50 million right now is sort of our minimum check size. And so where it made sense to hire a fund of funds manager as an example is we hired a venture seed fund of funds manager, where we could write them a $50 million check and then they could go out and write $5 million checks on our behalf to smaller seed funds.
turns.zh: 嗯，方向上是说得通的。我觉得现在 5,000 万美元大致就是我们的最低支票规模。举个聘用母基金管理人说得上划算的例子：我们聘了一家风险投资种子期母基金的管理人，我们可以给他们开一张 5,000 万美元的支票，然后他们再代表我们去给那些更小的种子基金开 500 万美元的支票。

turns.en: And so that was one area where it made sense. Now we're going to take a quick break to speak with our sponsor. On the show today, we have our stellar partner and industry expert, Shane Gowdy, leader of Sidley's Venture Funds Practice.
turns.zh: 所以那就是一个划算的领域。（接下来）我们先稍作休息，和我们的赞助商聊几句。今天来到节目中的，是我们出色的合作伙伴、行业专家 Shane Gowdy，他是 Sidley 律师事务所风险投资基金业务（Venture Funds Practice）的负责人。

turns.en: And now host of the podcast Talk VC, we highly recommend you listen. Your practice is concentrated on the fund formation and representation of venture capital and private equity funds, focusing on the fundraising side for a bit.
turns.zh: 他现在还是播客 Talk VC 的主持人，我们强烈建议大家去听听。你的业务集中在风险投资和私募股权基金的组建（fund formation）与代理上。我们先聊聊募资这一端。

turns.en: Has anything changed about how you're forming funds today versus a couple of years ago? Yeah, that's a great question. Yes and no. I think the main element, when I look at a brand new fund formation, I think is how can I be impactful not just from the blocking and tackling of the work, the drafting, the fund agreement, and looking at a PPM or a deck and doing all that great stuff.
turns.zh: 和几年前相比，你今天组建基金的方式有没有什么变化？嗯，这是个好问题。既有也没有。我觉得，当我面对一个全新的基金组建时，最核心的一点是：我怎么才能不只是在那些基础活儿上出力——起草文件、拟基金协议（fund agreement）、看私募备忘录（PPM）或路演材料、把这些漂亮活儿都做好。

turns.en: But it's just the value at impact of it. And so I think it's just being purpose driven about being proactive with the advice. I don't know if that's just more gray hairs on my face and on my head, or it's just the more practical approach that I think a lot of VCs want and need, in particular, emerging managers.
turns.zh: 而更在于价值和影响力。所以我觉得，关键在于带着目标感、主动地去给建议。我不知道这是因为我脸上、头上白头发多了，还是因为这本来就是更务实的做法——很多 VC 想要、也需要这种做法，尤其是那些新兴管理人（emerging managers）。

turns.en: A, they're cost sensitive, of course. And so I think what we really try to tailor our ability to do is meet that from an expectation and pricing standpoint.
turns.zh: 第一，他们当然对成本很敏感。所以我觉得我们真正努力去量身打造的，就是在预期和定价这两方面去满足他们。

turns.en: But just how we move in the project itself, it's trying to answer questions like, do we need a PPM? Nope, you don't need a PPM. And here's what it would cost you in hours for you and legal fees.
turns.zh: 而在项目本身怎么推进上，就是要去回答这样一些问题：我们需不需要一份 PPM？不需要，你用不着 PPM。而且做一份 PPM 会花掉你多少小时、多少律师费，我给你算清楚。

turns.en: And so I think it's really just trying to be incredibly helpful for and, again, proactive to help VCs understand what the choices they make during the fundraising.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，其实就是尽力做到极其有用，同时——再说一次——主动出击，帮 VC 们理解他们在募资过程中所做的每一个选择意味着什么。

turns.en: And that's not only just kind of what are the terms of the fund look like and what is the structure of the fund look like and kind of where the office is.
turns.zh: 这不仅仅是说基金的条款长什么样、结构长什么样、办公室设在哪里。

turns.en: And what is the fundraising strategy? Are you of an anchor investor? And are they going to proselytize it? So it's being just super involved in more of the business elements and the decision and the strategy.
turns.zh: 还包括募资策略是什么？你有没有一个锚定投资人（anchor investor）？他们会不会帮你去‘传道’、拉更多人进来？所以就是要深度参与到更多商业层面的要素、决策和战略里去。

turns.en: Now, that's always been something that I think has been present in every fund formation. But I would say that I have found that more water from the well is drawn by emerging managers on those just practical McKinsey like business consulting type of relationship and helping them steer the boat a lot with respect to that.
turns.zh: 这些东西我觉得在每一次基金组建中一直都存在。但我会说，我发现新兴管理人从这口井里打上来的水更多——他们更需要那种务实的、类似 McKinsey 式商业咨询的关系，需要你在掌舵这件事上多多帮他们把关。

turns.en: Now, much larger managers, they've just been around the block longer. And they usually have their own IR teams and their own ideas about how things will need to be constructed.
turns.zh: 至于那些规模大得多的管理人，他们见的世面更多、资历更老。他们通常有自己的投资者关系（IR）团队，对于事情该怎么搭建也有自己的一套想法。

turns.en: And we want to be receptive and open. But it's also still having a very active voice in those rooms as well. And it's a different game we play a lot in those kinds of funds because now we're dealing with government sovereigns and pension plans and university endowments and foundations.
turns.zh: 我们愿意接纳、保持开放。但同时在这些场合里也要有非常积极的话语权。在这类基金里，我们玩的是另一种游戏，因为现在我们打交道的是政府主权基金、养老金计划、大学捐赠基金和基金会。

turns.en: And it's being more prescient about how do they move through the world and the angulator of their atmosphere and how it hits you as opposed to more just venture 101, just kind of hand-holding, making sure that we go through the world.
turns.zh: 这就更需要有先见之明——去理解他们如何在世界上运作、他们所处环境的种种角度、以及这些会怎样影响到你；而不只是教‘风投入门 101’、手把手地带着走一遍流程。

turns.en: Because you're just not going to get the same kind of investor impact on the documents and everything else for maybe an emerging manager who's primarily high net worth and family office as opposed to a fund raising $500 million or $1 billion or $2 billion or whatever it looks like.
turns.zh: 因为，对于一个投资人主要是高净值人士和家族办公室（family office）的新兴管理人来说，你在文件和各方面受到的投资人影响，跟一个募资 5 亿、10 亿、20 亿美元或更大规模的基金，是完全不一样的。

turns.en: Your job is just different in that context. And it's being mindful and being ready to kind of, but also transmigrate lessons learned in both avenues to, hey, look, maybe have a little bit more of an emerging manager approach on some of this year.
turns.zh: 在那种情境下，你的工作性质就是不同的。你要保持警觉、做好准备，同时还要把两条路径上得到的经验教训融会贯通——嘿，看，今年在某些方面也许可以多一点新兴管理人的做法。

turns.en: The way in which you're talking to this LP really is even though you may have leverage, they're going to remember that the next fund. And so I think it's just, again, being incredibly prescient about being a business partner for me is what has changed in the last three, four, or five years.
turns.zh: 你和这个 LP 打交道的方式真的很关键——即便你手里有筹码，他们也会记着这件事，等到下一期基金的时候。所以我觉得，还是那句话：极其有先见之明地去做一个‘商业伙伴’，这就是过去三、四、五年里发生的变化。

turns.en: And I've seen VC's receptivity to it because they're being educated themselves about really good lawyers who do this work all the time. Like there, you could, again, draw so much water more from the well than just, hey, how do I put that in the partnership agreement?
turns.zh: 我也看到 VC 们越来越愿意接受这一点，因为他们自己也在被那些常年做这类工作的好律师‘科普’。你从这口井里能打上来的水，远不止是‘嘿，这条我该怎么写进合伙协议（partnership agreement）里’这么简单。

turns.en: And what does that subscription agreement look like? And help me draft this out. No, what do you think? What's your perspective? And that's how I choose what funds I want to work with is because they will want to have that dialogue and they will take that feedback and they will at least have a great amount of respect and self-reflection and understand where their own needs are.
turns.zh: 也不只是‘那份认购协议（subscription agreement）长什么样、帮我把这个起草出来’。而是‘你怎么看？你的观点是什么？’这也正是我挑选合作基金的方式——因为他们会愿意进行这样的对话，会接受反馈，至少会带着极大的尊重和自我反思，去搞清楚自己真正的需求在哪里。

turns.en: And like, look, it's nice one-stop shopping. And we also are very adamant about like introducing our emerging manager and other clients to LPs that we know are investing in the industry and that we've seen across.
turns.zh: 而且，你看，这种一站式服务很好。我们也非常坚定地去把我们服务的新兴管理人和其他客户，介绍给那些我们知道正在这个行业里投资、我们也打过交道的 LP。

turns.en: And so some of that is also like business development help for them. And so it's just become this holistic thing. And again, these elements have always been there, but I think it's more now than ever before being proactive about that approach and not being as reactive.
turns.zh: 所以这其中也包含帮他们做业务拓展（business development）。于是这就变成了一件整体性的事。再强调一次，这些要素一直都在，但我觉得，比起以往任何时候，现在更多的是主动去采取这种方式，而不是那么被动。

turns.en: And what would you tell a fund-one manager who might think they can't afford Sidley? Yeah, I would say don't ever think that because we, and because there are a ton of managers just say they're gonna do an angel-lister sidecar.
turns.zh: 那你会对一位觉得自己请不起 Sidley 的‘一期基金’（fund-one）管理人说什么？嗯，我会说：千万别这么想。因为有太多管理人一上来就说，他们就打算做一个 AngelList 的 sidecar（跟投载体）。

turns.en: So whatever they're going to do because they think it's just prohibitive cost, the right legal partner for you will make the right economic accommodations.
turns.zh: 所以不管他们打算怎么做——因为他们觉得成本实在高得离谱——但真正适合你的法律合作伙伴，会在经济条件上做出合理的通融。

turns.en: But they will also tell you like if they think you're badass crazy for your expectations that you want somebody who's gonna tell you I think you're badass crazy.
turns.zh: 但他们也会直说，如果他们觉得你的预期‘疯得离谱’——你本来就想要一个敢对你说‘我觉得你疯得离谱’的人。

turns.en: But I think that don't be afraid to ask for it and don't sell yourself short because having the right counsel in your deals says a lot about you.
turns.zh: 但我觉得，别害怕去开口要，也别小看自己，因为在你的交易里有合适的法律顾问，这本身就说明了你的很多分量。

turns.en: And your relative level of sophistication, like if Sidley's taking you on as a client, that means something to a lot of LPs. And family office or whether it's high net worth or frankly institutions, the more and more you get into the institutional waters, you're just gonna need a firm like us because we know what the playbook looks like.
turns.zh: 这也体现了你相对的成熟度。如果 Sidley 愿意接你这个客户，这对很多 LP 来说都是有分量的——无论是家族办公室、高净值人士，还是坦白说机构投资人。你越往机构的水域深处走，就越需要我们这样的律所，因为我们清楚那套‘打法手册’（playbook）长什么样。

turns.en: And just from a cost efficiency standpoint, there are many parts of Sidley which they have clients that are cost agnostic venturing one of those categories.
turns.zh: 而且单纯从成本效率的角度看，Sidley 有很多业务板块的客户是对成本无所谓的——而风险投资并不属于那一类。

turns.en: And so my business is also about being very price accommodating. It's having the collection of any invoices that's gonna happen only on a first closing and probably giving some pricing accommodations as we wrap up through some closings.
turns.zh: 所以我这块业务也非常注重在价格上给予通融。比如，任何发票的收取都只在首次关账（first closing）时才发生，而且在我们陆续完成几轮关账的过程中，很可能还会给出一些价格上的优惠。

turns.en: And so it's doing things that are very venturing. And because the way we look at these relationships is like we want them to be very big, juicy pieces of fruit for the entirety of our firm.
turns.zh: 所以这些都是很‘风投范儿’的做法。因为我们看待这些关系的方式是：我们希望它们能成为对整个律所来说都非常大、非常多汁的果实。

turns.en: We want not only to do the fund information work but we wanna do your deal work. And if you got a credit line that you need established, we can help you with that.
turns.zh: 我们不仅想做基金组建的工作，还想做你的交易（deal）业务。如果你需要设立一条信贷额度（credit line），我们也能帮你。

turns.en: If you got employment stuff going on, we can help you with that or litigation. And God forbid you get in some tax trouble or litigators or you need some regulatory, right?
turns.zh: 如果你有雇佣方面的事务，我们能帮你；诉讼也行。但愿别——万一你惹上了税务麻烦、需要打官司，或者需要一些监管合规方面的支持，对吧？

turns.en: So we're just very mindful about the holistic nature of the relationships we have with our clients and probably pricing accordingly on this very first intersection point that we're gonna have with them just so we could become a trusted partner for them.
turns.zh: 所以我们非常注重与客户关系的整体性，并且很可能在与他们第一次打交道的那个节点上，就据此来定价——就是为了能成为他们值得信赖的合作伙伴。

turns.en: And it's also being open to honest discussion about what you guys charge way too much for that side letter you negotiated, right? And knocking off some amount of it, right?
turns.zh: 而且还要乐于坦诚地讨论——比如‘你们帮谈那份附函（side letter）收得太贵了’，对吧？然后从中减掉一部分费用，对吧？

turns.en: Because this is a partnership that we have with our clients and if you don't view it that way, then you need to not be kind of be responsible for any billing relationship with any client.
turns.zh: 因为这是我们与客户之间的一种伙伴关系。如果你不这么看待它，那你就不该去负责任何客户的账单关系。

turns.en: So that for me is kind of some of the kitten caboodle of the secrets of success in this client relationship management stuff. Thank you for joining us on the show.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，这大致就是客户关系管理这门学问里成功秘诀的全部精华（the whole kit and caboodle）。谢谢你来到我们的节目。

turns.en: Shane, if you're a GP or LP looking for expert guidance on fund formation and venture capital legal matters, you can visit Sidley's website, s-i-d-l-e-y.com.
turns.zh: 谢谢 Shane。如果你是一位 GP 或 LP，正在为基金组建和风险投资法律事务寻求专业指导，可以访问 Sidley 的官网：s-i-d-l-e-y.com。

turns.en: And now back to our LP interview. Is there any, for other allocators who are leading plans, maybe they're new to venture as well, is there any advice you have for them on how to diligence, which fund to fund, or consultant to use?
turns.zh: 现在我们回到 LP 访谈。对于那些掌管着计划、也许在风投上也还是新手的其他配置者，你有什么建议给他们吗——比如怎么做尽调、投哪只基金、或者用哪家顾问？

turns.en: The consultant world's pretty small space. There's probably like, yeah, a dozen of them. And there's a lot of them that are all really good.
turns.zh: 顾问这个圈子其实很小。大概也就……嗯，十几家吧。而且其中很多都非常优秀。

turns.en: I think, yeah, maybe one area where we focused on in our selection was there are a lot of clients consultants nowadays that sell their own products, proprietary products.
turns.zh: 我觉得，嗯，也许我们在挑选时重点考量的一个方面是：现在很多顾问会卖他们自己的产品、自有品牌产品（proprietary products）。

turns.en: And so that could create a bit of a conflict. But I mean, I understand why they do it. Like, you know, it drives most of the revenue for them.
turns.zh: 所以这可能会造成一点利益冲突。但我是说，我理解他们为什么这么做。你知道的，这能给他们带来大部分收入。

turns.en: And then on like, diligence, fund managers, you know, we sort of just take the approach we like to see a track record. So I think doing emerging managers is a little tougher for us unless where we've done new products or strategies is where maybe it's a firm we've worked with and have built a relationship or know their track record and they're launching a new product is one area.
turns.zh: 然后在尽调基金管理人这块，我们基本上就是采取一种思路：我们想看到过往业绩记录（track record）。所以对我们来说，投新兴管理人会更难一些——除非是投新产品或新策略的情形，比如那是一家我们合作过、已经建立起关系、或者了解其过往业绩的公司，而他们正在推出一只新产品，这是一个例外领域。

turns.en: But yeah, we need some kind of track record to diligence, quantitatively. And then we'd like to see a stable team and skin in the game, GP commit, so.
turns.zh: 但是，对，我们需要有某种可以量化尽调的过往业绩记录。此外，我们还希望看到一支稳定的团队、以及‘利益绑定’（skin in the game），也就是 GP 的出资额（GP commit）。

turns.en: As a past wealth manager, Frank, I see these parallels where people say sort of the more you have, the more complexity that invites. And you are a very fascinating example of this, sort of comparing your average dentist's portfolio to this portfolio that you've inherited where you are in the process of adding these alts.
turns.zh: Frank，作为一名曾经做过财富管理的人，我看到了这些相似之处——人们常说，你拥有的越多，随之而来的复杂性就越多。而你就是一个非常有趣的例子：把一个普通牙医的投资组合，和你接手的这个组合相比——你正在往里面加入这些另类资产。

turns.en: And I think that's sort of happening to high net worths in droves right now, but they are also sort of thinking strategically about how to do this.
turns.zh: 我觉得现在成群的高净值人士正在经历类似的情况，但他们也在从战略层面思考该怎么去做这件事。

turns.en: Given that you have both worked as a wealth manager and now are managing nine billion, what can folks take for their own personal wealth management from this strategy?
turns.zh: 既然你既做过财富管理，如今又在管理 90 亿美元，那么普通人在自己的个人财富管理上，能从这套策略里借鉴些什么？

turns.en: Like what is the point of alternatives? Is this, does this belong in the dentist's portfolio or is there a reason you're adding it and they shouldn't?
turns.zh: 比如说，另类资产的意义到底是什么？它该不该出现在那个牙医的组合里？还是说，你之所以要加它、是有原因的，而他们不该加？

turns.en: Yeah, that's a great question. I think one of the, well, first of all, one of the biggest differences between like high net worth investing and institutional investing is, in high net worth investing, I think your primary focus is tax awareness.
turns.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题。我觉得……首先，高净值投资和机构投资之间最大的区别之一在于：在高净值投资里，我认为你的首要关注点是税务意识（tax awareness）。

turns.en: Whereas we're tax exempt, so we don't think about that. We're more like benchmark awareness. When I was in private wealth, nobody really cared about benchmarks, they just cared about mitigating taxes, right?
turns.zh: 而我们是免税的，所以我们不考虑这个。我们更多是基准意识（benchmark awareness）。我做私人财富管理那会儿，没人真的在意基准，他们只在意怎么少缴税，对吧？

turns.en: And so that's, I think the first step to like understand that different lens. But then also time horizon is really important because when you're talking about personal net worth or family money, like there is always going to be liquidity events, whether that's birth of a child, death of a family member, marriage, and you're always going to need liquidity.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，第一步是要理解这种不同的视角。此外，投资期限（time horizon）也非常重要，因为当你谈到个人财富或家族的钱时，总会遇到流动性事件——不管是孩子出生、家人离世，还是结婚——你总是需要流动性。

turns.en: And so there are a lot of these like private funds moving into raising retail money. And even if you're like ultra high net worth, I would say locking up capital for a decade, it should probably be a very small part of your portfolio.
turns.zh: 所以现在有很多私募基金开始转向募集零售（retail）资金。而我想说，即便你是超高净值人士，把资金锁定十年，这部分在你组合里也应该占很小很小的比例。

turns.en: You spoke about when you first jumped into investing overall, or sorry, you jumped into the real estate space and things kind of went down. Is there anything in similarities and just now that you're a real macroeconomic person that you're seeing in similarities from that GFC to now and how that's impacting your decisions on which asset classes to invest in?
turns.zh: 你刚才聊到你最初踏入投资、哦不对，是你踏入房地产那会儿，行情一路往下走。如今你已经是个十足的宏观经济观察者了，你有没有看到从当年那场全球金融危机到现在有什么相似之处？这些相似点又是如何影响你在‘投哪些资产类别’上的决策的？

turns.en: You know what, obviously like hindsight's 2020 and none of us have the crystal ball, but I think maybe the one way I think about it is like, as there's this saying bull markets climb the wall of worry.
turns.zh: 这么说吧，显然事后诸葛亮谁都会当，我们谁也没有水晶球。但我觉得，我思考它的一个方式是——有句老话讲，牛市是‘爬着担忧之墙’（climb the wall of worry）往上走的。

turns.en: So as long as there's like healthy skepticism, we could probably like just keep marching higher. And it's really when that's kept, like cause you still see like there's thought pieces and articles that come out every day that are like, is this an AI bubble?
turns.zh: 所以只要还存在健康的怀疑情绪，我们大概就能继续往上走。真正该警惕的是当这种怀疑消失的时候——因为你现在每天还能看到各种评论文章在问：这是不是又一个 AI 泡沫？

turns.en: As long as those articles are coming out, I think we're safe. Like when those articles stop coming out, that's when you should start worrying.
turns.zh: 只要这类文章还在不断冒出来，我觉得我们就还安全。等哪天这些文章都不再出现了，那才是你该开始担心的时候。

turns.en: Yeah, no one saw it coming, interesting. Yeah, so, but yeah, and for us, it's just so impossible to market time. So we have to just stay invested and figure out ways to, we do use a lot of long short strategies.
turns.zh: 嗯，没人能预料到，有意思。对，不过话说回来，对我们而言，择时（market timing）几乎是不可能的。所以我们只能一直保持投资状态，然后想办法……我们确实用了很多多空策略。

turns.en: So we could at least like pick up some P and L on the short side during bear markets. And you probably are paying a lot of attention to the energy markets as well.
turns.zh: 这样在熊市里，我们至少能从做空这一端赚到一些盈亏（P&L）。而且你多半也非常关注能源市场。

turns.en: Is there anything, I don't think we've had anybody who's quite so close to the energy world as you on the show. Anything sort of that you see from your seat that other folks don't recognize?
turns.zh: 有没有什么……我觉得我们节目还没请过像你这样离能源世界如此近的人。有没有什么是你从自己的位置上能看到、而其他人没意识到的？

turns.en: You know what? Like I don't like have my fingers on the pulse of like the oil and gas market day to day, but we have been moving more, shifting our real assets book like from real estate to infrastructure.
turns.zh: 这么说吧，我并不是天天盯着油气市场的脉搏，但我们确实一直在更多地调整我们的实物资产（real assets）组合——从房地产转向基础设施（infrastructure）。

turns.en: So we're building out our infrastructure portfolio, which includes things like energy, transportation, data centers and so I think with the continued build out of data centers, there is gonna be just a huge demand for energy going forward.
turns.zh: 所以我们正在扩充基础设施组合，里面包括能源、交通运输、数据中心等等。我觉得，随着数据中心持续扩建，未来对能源的需求会非常巨大。

turns.en: And so, and those types of trends are secular. Like they're not something that like, when you're investing in public stocks, small caps could be in favor this month and how to favor next month.
turns.zh: 而这类趋势是长期结构性的（secular）。它们不像你投公开市场股票那样——小盘股这个月受青睐，下个月又不受青睐了。

turns.en: These kinds of trends are like a decade long. So if you think like, oh, we're late to the game, like I'm pretty sure you're not. How do you tell the difference, Frank, between what's a way to diagnose if you're in a 10-year investment cycle versus a psycho-mediatrip investment cycle?
turns.zh: 这类趋势往往长达十年。所以如果你想‘哦，我们入场太晚了’，我基本可以肯定你并没有晚。Frank，那你怎么去区分、怎么去判断，你身处的是一个 10 年的投资周期，还是一个被情绪和媒体左右的短期投资周期？

turns.en: How, what are the distinctions for you? Well, I guess, you know, what I was referring to is in real assets, even if you think about real estate, like the Amazon effect of like industrial real estate, dominating retail real estate, like that has gone on for a decade and it's still happening, right?
turns.zh: 对你来说，两者的区别在哪儿？嗯，我想，你知道，我指的是实物资产这一块。就算只看房地产——比如‘Amazon 效应’让工业地产压过零售地产——这已经持续了十年，而且还在继续，对吧？

turns.en: And so that's sort of like a secular trend that's not going away. And I think this data center build out with energy demand is gonna be very similar.
turns.zh: 所以那是一种不会消失的长期结构性趋势。我觉得这一轮数据中心扩建、连同随之而来的能源需求，会非常相似。

turns.en: Yeah, our use of CHEP GPT and CLOT is not going anywhere. Interestingly, cool fact, half of token usage is consumer. So despite Anthropic being sort of heralded as like the very clever part player to go enterprise first, consumers are using just as many queries.
turns.zh: 对，我们对 ChatGPT 和 Claude 的使用是不会消退的。有意思的是——说个冷知识：一半的 token 使用量来自消费者端。所以，尽管 Anthropic 被誉为那种非常聪明、走‘企业优先’路线的玩家，消费者发出的查询量却一样多。

turns.en: Well, yeah, that is interesting. It'd be interesting to see like where the like geography is coming from, like if half of that is coming out of Silicon Valley.
turns.zh: 嗯，对，这确实有意思。要是能看看这些用量在地域上是从哪儿来的，会很有意思——比如其中一半是不是都来自 Silicon Valley。

turns.en: Yeah, we all have our personal accounts at our work accounts, I guess. It's probably, yeah, we're probably doing work from our computers on our personal computers and then copying and pasting.
turns.zh: 是啊，我猜我们既有个人账户、也有工作账户。很可能……对，我们多半是在用个人电脑办公，然后再复制粘贴来复制粘贴去。

turns.en: I know we don't have the crystal balls, but where do you see public plans going? Because not all are moving in the same direction. Where do you see that, what are gonna be some of the results and outcomes for the different public plans because a lot of states have different situations going on?
turns.zh: 我知道我们没有水晶球，但你觉得公共计划未来会往哪走？因为它们并不都朝着同一个方向前进。你怎么看——不同的公共计划会各自出现什么样的结果和成效？毕竟很多州的处境都不一样。

turns.en: Yeah, their private markets has been around a while at least like private equity in real estate. Public plans move slow. So I know there's a lot of public plans that still haven't even like started a private credit book or an infrastructure book, like and they were because we all think about things in the strategic asset allocation buckets, you know, they haven't approved, if you haven't approved like a private credit bucket
turns.zh: 嗯，私募市场已经存在一段时间了，至少私募股权和房地产是这样。公共计划行动很慢。所以我知道，有很多公共计划甚至还没开始建立私募信贷（private credit）组合或基础设施组合——因为我们都习惯按战略资产配置（strategic asset allocation）的桶来思考问题。如果他们还没批准——如果你还没批准设立一个私募信贷的桶，

turns.en: then you're kind of just like, well, where do we put this? And so I talked to a lot of other allocators who they have like an opportunistic bucket and they kind of just like throw hedge funds and private credit in that same bucket.
turns.zh: 那你就会有点犯难：那……我们把这个放哪儿呢？我和很多其他配置者聊过，他们有一个机会型（opportunistic）桶，就把对冲基金和私募信贷一股脑都扔进同一个桶里。

turns.en: So I think maybe going forward, some plans will start to sort of set up those dedicated allocation buckets too and start leaning into private credit and infrastructure.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，往后看，一些计划也会开始设立这些专门的配置桶，开始加码私募信贷和基础设施。

turns.en: And, you know, there are some plans that don't do any private still. They take the, you know, 60, 40 liquid approach and that's fine too. I think a lot of those plans are sort of similar like us where they're like really lean staff and that's why they stick to the liquid 60, 40 approach.
turns.zh: 而且，你知道的，也有些计划完全不做私募。他们采取那种 60/40 的流动性方案，这也挺好。我觉得这些计划里有很多和我们类似——人员非常精简，所以他们才坚持用流动性高的 60/40 方案。

turns.en: I've been trying to, I guess, challenge that and say like, how do I move into private markets but still, yeah, keep it really simple. I have like many follow-ups to that because it starts to unpack for those who have never approached or pitched pension funds and that, you know, this unique animal, like most emerging managers who are listening to this show, they are familiar with or, you know, maybe institutional investors who are not taxing,
turns.zh: 我一直在试着——我猜——去挑战这一点，问自己：我要怎么进入私募市场，同时又保持得非常简单。关于这个我有很多追问，因为对于从没接触过、也没向养老基金融过资的人来说，这里面门道很多。养老金是一种很独特的‘物种’。大多数在听这期节目的新兴管理人，可能对机构投资人、以及这一套并不那么熟悉。

turns.en: not, not, sorry, tax neutral. Except. Except, thank you very much. The history is very fascinating. Would you mind giving, like, is there any other examples sort of of the historical role of alternatives that you can give us?
turns.zh: 不、不，抱歉——是税务中性（tax neutral）……算了算了，非常感谢。这段历史非常有意思。你介意再给我们举些例子吗——另类资产在历史上扮演过哪些角色，还有没有别的例子？

turns.en: Because I think it just helps give more context as these managers are sort of going upstream speaking to bigger institutions. You know, a lot of pensions historically, like they weren't really, it was like one accountant that was managing the pension fund and it was all like bonds.
turns.zh: 因为我觉得，这能提供更多背景，帮助这些管理人在‘向上游走’、去接触更大的机构时更有底气。你知道的，历史上很多养老金——它们其实谈不上有多专业，往往就是一个会计在管着养老基金，而且全都是债券。

turns.en: That was how like almost all these pensions started back, you know, back like in the glory days of when interest rates were like 20% in like late 70s, early 80s, but yeah, they, as I mentioned, they had to start taking more risk to hit their hurdle rate.
turns.zh: 几乎所有这些养老金当初就是这么起步的——回到那个‘黄金年代’，也就是 70 年代末、80 年代初，利率高达 20% 的时候。但是，嗯，就像我提到的，它们后来不得不开始承担更多风险，才能达到它们的门槛收益率（hurdle rate）。

turns.en: So they started like building out these investment offices and pursuing equities and pursuing alts. And so the, yeah, the industry has evolved where a lot, you know, a lot of plans are now, alts have become a main part of the portfolio.
turns.zh: 于是它们开始搭建投资办公室、开始配置股票、开始追逐另类资产。所以，yeah，这个行业一直在演进——如今对很多计划来说，另类资产已经成为组合里的主要组成部分。

turns.en: And I guess the other part of your question was around like how the GPs should think about it when they're approaching them. Yeah, if you realize that you are part of a potentially very new, like this is sort of something that everybody's just getting rolling on.
turns.zh: 我猜你问题的另一部分是关于 GP 在接触这些机构时该怎么想。对，如果你意识到，自己正身处一个可能非常新的领域——这是大家才刚刚开始上手的东西。

turns.en: I'm curious if you even can share like which are some of the pensions that are just dipping a toe versus are more like, well, have a long standing history in venture.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，你能不能分享一下：哪些养老金只是刚‘探个脚趾头’试水，哪些则在风投上有着悠久的历史？

turns.en: I think actually more of the university endowments have been in venture the longest, right? Like the, you know, with Dave Swanson and the Yale model kind of kicking it off in the 80s.
turns.zh: 我觉得其实是大学捐赠基金做风投的时间最长，对吧？比如，你知道的，Dave Swensen 和那个‘Yale 模式’（Yale model），大致是在 80 年代开启的。

turns.en: And I think that's... They kind of popularized it, sure. Yeah, but I think a lot of pensions have adopted it as well. And maybe, you know, it's more about like the amount of allocation, like I know some endowments, they're like 50% private equity and venture capital, whereas most pensions, they kind of, I would say they're more like 20% private.
turns.zh: 我觉得那……他们算是把它带火了，没错。对，但我觉得很多养老金也采纳了这套做法。也许，你知道的，差别更多在于配置的比例——我认识一些捐赠基金，它们有 50% 配在私募股权和风险投资上；而大多数养老金，我会说它们的私募配置更像是 20% 左右。

turns.en: The way we think about it is we call, when we say private equity, venture capital lives under that bucket. And so it's like buyout and venture.
turns.zh: 我们的思路是：当我们说‘私募股权’时，风险投资是归在这个桶下面的。所以它包含并购（buyout）和风投（venture）。

turns.en: And I think a lot of allocators maybe think about it as like a two thirds, one third split. I guess it could be different from shop to shop, but so yeah, if you've got, you know, so maybe like most pensions are probably only like 5%, 5% venture capital.
turns.zh: 我觉得很多配置者可能会按‘三分之二、三分之一’的比例来划分。我猜各家机构可能不一样，但所以，嗯，如果你……你知道的，也许大多数养老金的风投配置大概只有 5%、5% 左右。

turns.en: Frank, my last question is around, and you can go anywhere. We've had a few CIOs who've remind us venture capitalists that there are other asset classes out there.
turns.zh: Frank，我的最后一个问题是——你可以随便聊。我们请过几位 CIO，他们提醒我们这些做风险投资的人：这世上还有别的资产类别呢。

turns.en: I can't believe it, but apparently there are. Curious, what strategies do you wish you saw more of? It doesn't have to be inventor, it can be in any, like which strategies, as far as fund managers, do you wish you saw more of, that you think some real opportunity is being missed?
turns.zh: 我简直不敢相信，但看来确实有。我很好奇：你希望看到更多哪类策略？不一定非得是风投，可以是任何领域——就基金管理人而言，你希望看到更多哪些策略、觉得其中正错失真正的机会？

turns.en: What I'm seeing a lot of right now in terms of like, you know, I do get a lot of in bounds. I would say right, like right now, I feel like 75% of the in bounds I get are private credit.
turns.zh: 就我现在看到的大量项目而言——你知道的，我确实收到很多主动上门的项目（inbounds）。我会说，眼下我觉得我收到的项目里有 75% 都是私募信贷。

turns.en: Yeah, and we're at a point in our private credit book where we're overweight and trimming. And so, you know, I'm basically not even thinking about private credit.
turns.zh: 对，而我们的私募信贷组合已经到了超配、正在减仓的阶段。所以，你知道的，我基本上现在连想都不去想私募信贷了。

turns.en: And so, what I wish I saw more of, I feel like I see plenty of everything. And there's not, you know, I guess there are like, we don't do a lot of like niche esoteric strategies, but like for example, like within private credit, there's that sort of bank risk sharing.
turns.zh: 所以说，我希望看到更多什么呢？我觉得各类项目我都见得够多了。也没有什么……我猜也有一些——我们不太做那种小众、冷僻的策略。但比如说，在私募信贷里面，有一类是银行风险分担（bank risk sharing）。

turns.en: And there's a lot of like, there's some strategies out there that are dedicated to that. And but we haven't done anything direct like that. We're just sort of taking the diversified approach to asset-backed lending.
turns.zh: 市面上有不少专门做这个的策略。但我们自己还没直接做过那样的东西。我们只是对资产支持贷款（asset-backed lending）采取了分散化的方式。

turns.en: I guess maybe like sports is sports private, equity is sort of becoming popularized now. And, you know, I'm curious to see how that evolves where some of the leagues are very exclusive with who they invite in to allow as investors.
turns.zh: 我猜，也许像体育——体育私募股权现在正变得流行起来。你知道的，我很好奇这会怎么演变，因为有些联赛对于能邀请谁进来、允许谁当投资人，是非常挑剔、非常排他的。

turns.en: And like, I wonder, you know, everyone I talk to says like these sports teams are, like the valuations are too high. It doesn't make sense. But then you think about like, well, the TAM is barely tapped where now leagues are talking about like marketing global league like beyond the US.
turns.zh: 我就在想，你知道的，我聊过的每个人都说，这些体育队伍的估值太高了、说不通。但你再想想：这块潜在市场（TAM）其实几乎还没被开发——如今各联赛都在谈论怎么把联赛营销到美国以外的全球市场。

turns.en: But then also like, what happens if, and I don't know if this will ever happen, but like what happens if the leagues do like lower the gate and say, hey, all private equity is welcome to invest.
